safe.label: He tells the woman who loves him to run away fast
safe.note: The chorus is an instruction, not a plea. Leaving is presented as her best available option and he is the one supplying the plan.

safe.label: He always finds something wrong right when it starts working
safe.note: Not drift, a pattern. She has been putting up with it way too long, which means the sabotage has a track record.

real.label: He'd rather be the villain who warned her than explain the emails
real.note: Run away is a confession he can perform without giving details. Blanket guilt costs him less than one specific accounting of what he did.

safe.label: A toast to the douchebags, and he raises it about himself
safe.note: The song opens by naming a category of bad men and volunteering for it. Public self-indictment delivered as a party toast.

real.label: If he accuses himself first nobody else gets to land it
real.note: The toast is armor. Naming himself scumbag in public means every future accusation arrives as old news he already made into a hook.

safe.label: Never much of a romantic, never could take the intimacy
safe.note: Stated as a fixed trait rather than a wound. Closeness registers as something he cannot metabolize, like a capacity he was born without.

safe.label: The fame rewards exactly the behavior that ruins the relationship
safe.note: Being the guy everyone talks about is the job. The traits that make the career work are the traits she has to survive.

real.label: Intimacy has no scoreboard so he cannot tell if he is winning
real.note: Everywhere else he can measure himself. With her there is nothing to beat, no number going up, and being unmeasured feels indistinguishable from being nothing.

links.rationale: Moves the toast from confession to strategy: he is not admitting he is a douchebag, he is claiming the title before anyone can pin it on him

links.rationale: Names what the instruction to leave is actually protecting, not her, but him from having to say out loud what she already found
